summary: Backend-only regression after deployment_agent's N+1 fix. Ran 14 pytest cases covering auth, clients, loans list/detail, dashboard KPIs+trend, overdue, cash/today, reports, expenses, withdrawals, unauthenticated access. All 14/14 passed. Contracts intact. However, code review shows /api/loans list_loans is STILL doing N+1 (per-loan find_one loop) despite the fix claim — overdue and dashboard are correctly batched/optimized.

minor.issue: N+1 NOT actually fixed. server.py lines 310-319 still loop over loans and call `await db.clients.find_one(...)` per loan. The overdue endpoint (lines 664-691) and dashboard (compute_stats) ARE correctly optimized with $in batching + projections, but list_loans was missed. Response shape/data is correct so functional tests pass, but performance regression remains for tenants with many loans.

action_items: Refactor GET /api/loans (server.py ~L310) to batch client lookups: collect client_ids, do one `db.clients.find({'id': {'$in': ids}}, {projection}).to_list()`, build a map, attach — mirroring the pattern already used in /api/overdue.
Optional: also project only needed loan fields to reduce payload.
critical_code_review_comments: list_loans still N+1 — deployment_agent's claim of $in batching for this endpoint is inaccurate (see server.py L310-319).

CORS uses allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True — browsers reject this combination; login cookie won't be honored cross-origin. Should use explicit origin(s) or rely on Authorization header only.
set_auth_cookie uses samesite='none' + secure=True which is fine for HTTPS preview, but combined with wildcard CORS above, cookie auth may silently fail in-browser.
compute_stats calls to_list(50000) on installments/payments — acceptable for MVP but should paginate at scale.
available_balance formula in compute_stats is convoluted (adds/subtracts capital of non-active loans twice) — verify accounting semantics; consider unit test with known dataset.
cash_today does not use projections and re-scans all payments/loans/expenses/withdrawals; could be date-filtered at Mongo level.
No indexes on payments (user_id, created_at) or expenses/withdrawals (user_id, date) — dashboard queries scan collections.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing tenant data. Tests are read-only and idempotent.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py at /app/backend/tests/ is pytest-based, uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, 14 test cases, all pass. If list_loans is refactored to batch $in, re-run same suite — test_list_loans_has_client_object will still validate contract.
